verdict.rationale: Mastra Code documents recurring prompts that can be created, run, paused, resumed, or deleted, which is a native recurring-schedule capability. Goals keep the agent working across turns until a judge model marks the objective complete, and headless mode with auto-approval supports unattended runs. Event-based triggers are not a documented product feature: CI embedding is only a building block the user would wire up, and there is no evidence that recurring prompts run always-on outside an active session. Missing for 10: documented native triggers (events, webhooks, repo events), evidence that schedules persist as always-on background agents, in-depth docs on recurring-prompt scheduling, and independent or hands-on corroboration of autonomous maintenance and fixing.

support.subject: As an ai-native user, I can set up always-on agents that run on schedules or triggers to maintain and fix my software autonomously

citations.quote: Create, run, pause, resume, or delete recurring prompts
Keep Mastra Code working across turns until a judge model marks the objective complete or waits for your input.
